cards.title: My son is leaving home for university
cards.body: A parent reflects on the emotional challenges of empty nesting as their eldest heads off to start university. While often portrayed as natural, the experience of letting go can be surprisingly difficult and worth acknowledging.

cards.title: Second baby parenting feels like starting over
cards.body: A parent admits to forgetting much about infant care between children—from feeding to teething to sleep schedules. With help from family, they're rediscovering both parenting basics and memories of their own relaxed childhood.

cards.title: Should AI really do the parenting work?
cards.body: Tech companies peddle eye-movement trackers and nap-prediction apps, but parenting is already an unpaid job—do we need to over-optimize it further? The question raises real concerns about tech replacing human connection in child-rearing.

cards.title: The '18 summers' parenting trend unpacked
cards.body: This trend turns summer freedom into scheduled 'memory-making' exercises, removing the unstructured boredom that defines childhood. Critics argue it's controlling and creepy—missing the actual point of downtime.

cards.title: Afterschool meltdowns: Supporting neurodivergent kids
cards.body: Many neurodivergent children and teens struggle with afterschool shutdowns and meltdowns as they transition between environments. Parents and schools can work together to provide targeted support and reduce stress.

cards.title: What is a parent's job, really?
cards.body: Rather than guaranteeing happiness and success, a parent's true role is building character, resilience, and resources in their children. This reframe shifts focus from outcomes to long-term capability.

cards.title: When your adult child needs you as the villain
cards.body: Even after apologizing and changing, some adult children still need a parent to remain the 'bad guy' in their family narrative. Understanding this emotional need can help parents navigate complex adult relationships.

cards.title: 'Mommy, I'm bored': Summer boredom as opportunity
cards.body: When kids complain of boredom during summer, they're often signaling a genuine need for guidance and engagement. Parents can reframe these moments as chances to teach self-motivation and problem-solving.

cards.title: Exercise improves depression and anxiety in youth
cards.body: A study of 38,000 children and adolescents confirms that physical activity meaningfully reduces symptoms of depression and anxiety. This evidence-based finding offers parents a practical tool for supporting mental health.

cards.title: Empty nesting often begins before kids leave
cards.body: Parents may start grieving the separation months before their child actually leaves, as imagining the change makes it emotionally real. Recognizing this anticipatory sadness as normal can help families prepare.

cards.title: Donor conception and the fear of belonging
cards.body: Children born through donor conception may struggle with identity, attachment, and feelings of not belonging within their family story. Understanding how genetic loss shapes development helps families address these complex emotions.

cards.title: Autism is not a crutch or overdiagnosis
cards.body: Giftedness can mask autism in children, and dismissing it as overdiagnosed or a crutch erases real support needs. Parents of autistic children should recognize the genuine complexity of the condition.

cards.title: IVF families fear wrong donors were used
cards.body: Multiple families report that fertility clinics may have used different sperm and egg donors than they originally selected. This breach of consent raises serious ethical and legal concerns for families.
